findings.where: Screen 6 (On the work), text and the say line
findings.what: No screen says why there is spare oil, and a steps lesson shows only the frame, so the explain never reaches him: say that this pump pushes out the same amount every turn and the slowed cylinder takes less, so the pressure rises until the relief valve opens. Without that, the relief line lit and the needle on the relief mark while the ram is still moving go unexplained.

findings.where: Screen 6 (On the work), text plus the say line
findings.what: While the ram comes down the screen carries about 102 words (55 in the text and 47 in the say line), over the 90-word limit; drop 'When the ram stops on the work, all the pump's oil goes that way', because the say line says it once the ram stops, and that also makes room for the fixed-pump sentence.

findings.where: Screen 10 (The same job in air), text plus the say line
findings.what: With -Y3 on and the slider moved the screen carries about 110 words (54 above the picture, 56 below it), and 98 at rest, which is the 'too much text after the diagrams' Dan objected to; cut the squeeze-test half of the say line down to one short sentence such as 'The air gives and the oil does not.', because the readout already shows the volume.

findings.where: Screen 8 (Back up), text plus the say line
findings.what: The screen runs to 95-99 words (56 in the text plus 39-43 in the say line), over about 90; cut 'Switch -Y2 off and the middle box blocks A and B. The ram holds.', because the say line says exactly this once both solenoids are off.

findings.where: Screen 9 (Into the rod side), the picture before Check
findings.what: -Y2 is drawn energised while the middle box still sits against the ports, so the picture breaks the rule screens 4 and 8 just taught, and a careful reader who reads that box sees B blocked and is drawn to 'It cannot'; slide the row to the crossed box before Check and keep only the lines idle until the answer.

Two of the three footnotes sit on plain descriptions of how the circuit works ('the other is lined up to drain back to the tank', 'the rod side is exhausted'), not on a rule or value he would look up on a job; keep only [^1], on the drawn-state rule.

findings.where: Screen 13 (Safe to open?), the picture before Check
findings.what: The A line is already red and labelled 'still under pressure' before he answers, so he answers from the label rather than by reading that the middle box blocks A; draw the line plain until Check and let the red come in with the pulse.

findings.where: Screen 7 (What sets the squeeze?), the picture before Check
findings.what: Before he answers, the relief path is lit, the needle sits on the relief mark and the caption reads 'The pump's oil is going over the relief valve.', and screen 6's last sentence has just given the answer, so the puzzle only tests recall of one sentence; keep the lines idle and hide the caption until Check.

Before he taps Stop, the text says the valve 'centred' and the line 'is drawn red', but -Y1 is still on and nothing is red, and no screen says that Stop switches both solenoids off, which is why the valve centres; lead with the cause, for example 'Stop stops the pump and switches both solenoids off. The springs centre the valve while the ram still presses the work.'

No screen marks a key term in amber, and the lesson's three terms (flow path, exhaust port, stored energy) live only in the explain, which a steps lesson does not show; mark *exhaust port* on screen 10 and *stored energy* on screen 12 or 13, where he will meet them on an isolation.

findings.where: Every puzzle screen at 360 px (the screen 14 picture, and the 1280 px one too)
findings.what: The hidden switch block keeps its space before Check, leaving about 180 px of blank between the drawing and the answers and pushing the choices below the fold on a phone; reserve less height, or let the switches grow in after the answer.
The read opens 'Here -Y2 is on', but the still shows both solenoids off with the ram held part way; start the read with the state the picture shows.

findings.where: Explain text, the flow path sentence and the fixed pump sentence
findings.what: 'Each position gives the oil one route, from the pump through the cylinder and back to the tank' is untrue for the middle box (P to T, no cylinder) and for the descent (spare oil also goes over the relief valve), and 'pushes out the same oil every turn' should read 'the same amount of oil'.
The dashed mark is labelled 'at 6 bar' while every other pressure on the card is 'bar absolute'; say 'at 6 bar absolute' or just 'at the start'.

findings.where: Press key, all press screens at 360 px
findings.what: The 'Oil flowing' and 'Spare oil' arrows in the key differ only in stroke weight (3 against 1.8) and look almost the same on a phone; make the spare-oil line visibly thinner or dashed.

The gauge is drawn with no needle because the screen hides all flow, so the press 'at rest, with every part named' shows a gauge that looks broken; draw the needle near zero here, since there is no question to give away.
The button still reads 'Stop' when tapping it restarts the pump; a 'Start' label while the pump is stopped would need no say line to explain it.
